summary: Snohomish County, WA: 20-ft pole L-4 training tower built 1935 by the USFS; WWII AWS post 1942-43; sold and removed 1955; site not confirmed and no source describes it today.

facts.status_note: Sold and removed in 1955 by a private party for a vacation cabin (Register, firelookout.com, Willhite, Forest Lookouts). Willhite could not find the exact spot after two visits and says the site may be totally gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and firelookout.com give 1,225 ft (373 m); Willhite's notes say about 1,120 ft. The record's 373.4 m is kept and the disagreement is stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: The 1935 build, the training use, the 1942-43 AWS activation and the 1955 removal are each supported by at least two sources, though three of the four lookout pages draw on the same register data. Willhite is the only source with a site-level account, and he could not find the spot after two visits. No source describes what remains or whether the site is open today, so access is left out of facts. Willhite spells the place both Whitechuck and White Chuck and notes a 1930s map labelled the lookout Black Oak; the story uses Whitechuck Bench as the record does. The brief's record is consistent with the sources (coordinates and 373 m elevation match the Register), so no corrections are proposed. Used 5 page reads and 0 WebSearch calls.
